claims.text: Traditional single-phase ZrB2 requires processing above 2300 °C.
Reactive Si and C precursors will form a thin SiC interphase on ZrB2 particle surfaces and grain boundaries during spark plasma sintering at approximately 1700 °C.
The proposed precursor treatment may instead produce a borosilicate-like coating.
The in situ interphase will be thin, uniform, and coherent at ZrB2 grain boundaries.
An intergranular secondary phase can assist densification by filling voids or facilitating sintering.
A coherent secondary-phase interface can improve interfacial adhesion.
The SiC interphase will reduce interfacial energy and sintering barriers in ZrB2.
The SiC interphase will enable effective ZrB2 densification at approximately 1700 °C.
The SiC interphase will impede oxygen diffusion into the ZrB2 microstructure.
The SiC interphase will impede penetration of liquid plating metals into the ZrB2 microstructure.
The coated material will have mechanical strength and structural integrity comparable to or better than high-temperature-sintered single-phase ZrB2 and uncoated lower-temperature specimens.
The coated material will exhibit significantly less oxidation-scale growth than both comparison materials.
The coated material will exhibit significantly less liquid-metal penetration or corrosion damage than both comparison materials.
The proposed material is applicable in oxidizing atmospheres at temperatures up to approximately 1800 °C.
The proposed material is applicable for prolonged service in corrosive liquid plating-metal baths.

Interphase morphology, densification, strength, oxidation-scale thickness, and liquid-metal penetration can be compared against an identically processed uncoated control and a high-temperature benchmark.
Failure to achieve a predefined 10–20% improvement in the specified performance measures would falsify the hypothesis.
